topology_reasoning.description: Two-waveguide directional coupler with integrated grating couplers
structure: Upper waveguide: sharp entrance taper (point → core width)
Central grating region: periodic vertical teeth on both sides
Thin connecting bar between waveguides in grating section
Sharp exit tapers (core width → point) on both sides
function_defining_knobs: width_um: single waveguide core width (controls cross-sectional area)
gap_um: spacing between waveguide centerlines (controls coupling strength)
entrance_curve_length_um: length of entrance taper region
exit_curve_length_um: length of exit taper region
grating_pitch_um: period of grating teeth (spacing between teeth centers)
grating_duty_cycle: fill fraction of grating teeth (width_tooth / pitch)
grating_tooth_depth_um: perpendicular depth of teeth extending from core
topology_reasoning.physics: Directional coupler uses evanescent field overlap between parallel waveguides to enable mode exchange. Grating couplers provide efficient in/out coupling. The 0.7 μm height constraint fits a single channel width plus two waveguides with small gap.

iterations.change: Changed to triangular tapers instead of curves
Removed smooth curves, back to triangles
Reverted to two parallel waveguides with gap

notes: Best IoU achieved by understanding device as two-waveguide coupler rather than single waveguide. Parametric knobs successfully move geometry. Further improvement would require understanding target's exact curve topology (entrance/exit bends appear to be smooth S-curves rather than sharp tapers in the actual device).
